sections.title: Current conclusion
sections.markdown:
**31 October 2026:** The West Calder John is indexed as baptised on 6 September 1747, son of John Glasgow and Margaret Anderson: Findmypast OPR 701/1 item 5, p.51. This verifies the date as baptism in a derivative parish transcript, replacing the earlier index-unchecked qualification; the original still needs inspection and no exact birth is supplied. The adult John’s selected father remains 25%; the child’s recorded father remains 98%. The earlier sign-in/index-unchecked wording is historical and is superseded for this provider transcript, not for the original.

Current father assessment (22 October 2026): **98% (proved)** for [Glasgow-2847](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2847). Named child to the specific adult family role represented by the selected father; independent earlier ancestry is outside this assessment. This scoped assessment supersedes earlier grades for this parent pair; other identity questions remain as qualified below.

[John Glasgow of Larne (Glasgow-4179)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-4179) is now attached to [Hugh Glasgow (Glasgow-1499)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1499) as an **uncertain son**, with low confidence. This is a working hypothesis based on locality and generation, not a record naming his father. [Older William (Glasgow-1505)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1505) remains viable. No mother is attached; Hugh's wife Ann is not thereby identified as John's mother.

The duplicate marriage has been resolved: [Rose Allan (Allan-6611)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Allan-6611) is the wife of the Larne John, married in 1769 according to the [archived Kilwaughter/Larne chronology](https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html). Allan-8249 now redirects to Allan-6611, the older ID required by WikiTree. Both Rose profiles cited the same marriage; neither supplied an independent Rose baptism. Her estimated birth about 1750 and inferred County Antrim birthplace remain uncertain. The chronology's 1745–48 birth estimate concerns John, not Rose.

[John Glasgow of West Calder (Glasgow-2846)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2846), son of [John Glasgow (Glasgow-2847)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2847) and [Margaret Anderson](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Anderson-83671), remains a separate identity. Rose has been detached from him. The [1747 Scottish baptism citation](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-R5D) has not been re-inspected beyond the existing citation because FamilySearch requires sign-in. No inspected evidence joins that Scottish child to the Larne groom; this separation does not prove that they could never be the same man.

The original PRONI MIC/1B/6 marriage and baptism entries and the named lives in the 1751/1767 endorsements to lease D2977/3A/4/81/72A remain the tests for Hugh versus William. The [Larne memorial](https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt), pp.47–48, does not name John and is not proved to enumerate every surviving child.

potential_parentage.method: Automated leads use birth surnames—not married surnames—as parental eligibility, role-specific biological age limits, bounded and approximate-date uncertainty, household chronology, specific time-aware localities, mapped distance, tenancy succession, migration destinations and sex-aware Scottish naming positions across generations. People already attached as the subject's parents stay in the identity summary and are excluded from this alternative-candidate list, regardless of relationship confidence. The main calibration uses clues available on disconnected profiles; existing parent and sibling links are retained as comparison context rather than treated as transferable evidence. Common ordered names and grandparent-to-child echoes receive a small non-zero weight, so a John or James match can support several independent criteria without producing a lead alone. Rare names, repeated bearers and bundles across otherwise distinct branches receive substantially more weight according to catalogue frequency. An exact migration place is weighted by its rarity and repetition across both branches; a shared destination country is worth only one point. Extra weight is added only when at least three independent clue types converge: naming, locality, specific migration, household chronology or collateral networks. Sparse profiles retain a clearly labelled chronology-only fallback instead of disappearing. Countries, states, counties and research clusters do not count as a shared locality, and fallback, broad representative or kin-inferred coordinates are excluded from distance scoring. Shared descendant profiles are removed before branch-name comparison. A candidate already recorded as a parent-in-law is excluded. A confident or independently supported parent is treated as settled; uncertain and unassessed attachments remain open to alternative comparison. A different linked parent, an uncle/aunt or grandparent path, and a matching existing child profile prevent an alternative from being classified as a strong direct-parent lead until the underlying tree conflict or duplicate is resolved. Familiar forms such as Bessie are normalised. Surname remains an eligibility filter worth zero points.
potential_parentage.warning: Naming customs, shared farms and occupations are circumstantial. Children, spouses and collateral relatives may be missing, and tree-derived family networks are not independent evidence. Scores rank research leads; they do not prove parentage.

The adult John’s selected father remains 25%; the child’s recorded father remains 98%. The earlier sign-in/index-unchecked wording is historical and is superseded for this provider transcript, not for the original.

wikitree_comparison.remote_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' was a son of [[Glasgow-2847|John Glasgow]] and [[Anderson-83671|Margaret Anderson]], associated with a 1747 baptism at West Calder, Midlothian, Scotland.<ref name="Baptism">FamilySearch, "Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-R5D John Glasgow, 1747], cited for the son of John Glasgow and Margaret Anderson at West Calder. The original register entry has not been inspected in this research.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

'''Birth and baptism.''' His exact birth date is not established. The date 6 September 1747 needs checking against the baptism index and original register before it can be treated as an exact baptism date or used to establish a precise birth limit.<ref name="Baptism" />

'''Larne namesake.''' [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow of Larne]] married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] in 1769 according to the Kilwaughter/Larne family chronology. That chronology does not name the groom's parents or connect him to West Calder. No evidence identified here establishes that the Scottish child and the Larne groom were the same man; their identities remain separate.<ref name="Timeline">Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html "GLASGOWS from Kilwaughter Parish and Larne, County Antrim, Northern Ireland … Timeline"] (archived 24 November 2010), entry: "13. John3 Glasgow m. Rose Allan in 1769. Born perhaps 1745-48? Probably not the same as John2 who was a ship’s captain in 1739." This is evidence about the Larne groom, not proof of a marriage for the West Calder child.</ref>

== Sources ==
<references />
